# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Working Principles (user-mandated, 最高优先级)

用户时间与预算有限，**每个任务都必须为省时间/省 token 服务**：

- **最短路径**：只为当前任务做最小必要改动；不顺手重构、不新增无关文件、不写长篇注释或文档。
- **省 token 的读法**：先用 grep/glob 定位，再带 offset/limit 定点读；禁止重复整文件读取或整文件回显；改动优先用 edit，不要重写大文件。
- **少开 agent**：默认由 Lead 单独完成。只有当任务可拆成互不依赖的大块、且并行确实更快时才用 teammates；subagent 的上下文同样是成本。
- **验证从简**：本项目无测试套件，只做必要的最小验证（如 GDScript 语法/加载检查），不跑完整试玩流程，除非任务明确要求。
- **输出精简**：结论先行，只列改动点与验证结果，不复述代码。
- **任务完成必须弹 Windows 通知**：每次交付结束前执行
  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

</system-reminder>

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

    x = x - x.mean()
    y = y - y.mean()

    return float((x * y).sum() / d) if d > 0 else 0.0

找到根本原因了：它不是属性面板，就是**小地图的“底板”（地形底图）**在红方局被画到了小地图右下角。

**依据（对你截图的数值比对，非目测）**
- 截图里在小地图右下方、从 (490,490) 开始有一块 450×450 的深色方块，内部有一条斜向青色带。这块区域与小地图地形底图旋转 180° 后**相关系数为 0.999**，确认就是同一张底图，并非渲染场景。
- 450×450 正好等于小地图尺寸，偏移正好是 (+450,+450)：底图被“整块平移 + 旋转”，所以看起来像一块底板跑到了小地图外面。

**原因**
`MiniMap._draw()` 在红方局用 `Rect2(Vector2(S,S), Vector2(-S,-S))`（负尺寸）来翻转底图。在当前引擎里，负尺寸的 `draw_texture_rect` 不会原地翻转，而是把整张图画到 `(S,S)` 处再旋转 180°。我还用一张 450×450 的四色测试图单独验证了这一点：画出的方块确实落在 (450,450) 起的位置，内容是旋转 180° 的。

**为什么“又”错位**：开局 `Config.roll_player_team()` 会随机分配玩家阵营，**只有约 50% 的红方局**才走这条翻转分支，所以时好时坏。

**改动**：仅改 `MiniMap._draw()` 一处——红方改用 `draw_set_transform((S,S), PI)` 原地旋转再画，画完复位；不再使用负尺寸矩形，`_cache_static_map` 里的草丛和墙体本来就按翻转后的坐标烘焙，无需改动。

**验证**：强制红方阵营渲染一帧对战画面，同一 (490,490) 区域与底图的相关性从 0.999 降到 **-0.065**（底图不再外溢），小地图内 (40,40) 区域与底图相关性升到 0.552（底图回到框内）。无 `SCRIPT ERROR`、`Parse Error`。

另外提醒：你那张截图所在进程仍是旧构建（属性条还是 300 宽、没到我之前的加宽改动），**重开一局（红方局最容易复现）** 再看就能确认。[MiniMap.gd](scripts/ui/MiniMap.gd#L256-L263)

Task: 战场细节优化:
1. 防御塔外周的地面加上青砖质感 (tower surroundings: green-brick/stone pavement texture)
2. 草丛里面加入一些花 (flowers in bushes)

4. 墙上添加装饰 (decorations on walls)

Implementation should be in BattleManager._create_map / _add_wall_chain / turret creation / bushes. There are visual helper scripts: `scripts/core/MapVisuals.gd`, `scripts/entities/DecorMesh.gd`, `scripts/entities/WorldDecor.gd`, `scripts/entities/BushSway.gd`, `scripts/entities/TurretMesh.gd`, `scripts/entities/Wall.gd`.

Prefer simple: create a ring mesh (TorusMesh flattened? or CylinderMesh disc) with a procedurally generated brick texture? Simplest robust: use `PlaneMesh` with a StandardMaterial3D using a procedurally generated `ImageTexture` of green bricks, sized to the turret base radius, slightly above ground (y=0.02). - Wall decorations: add small ornaments on top (pillars caps, banner/vine spheres, torches?) — e.g., lantern-like glowing cubes at intervals along the wall, or moss/gold trim.

Bricks: 3 courses? Let's do: courses at radii 2.2, 3.2, 4.2 (with widths ~0.95 radial) → ring from 1.75 to 4.7. For each course, K = round(2πr / 0.75) bricks; each brick box size (tangential 0.62, height 0.07, radial 0.9), rotated to face outward, y ~0.03-0.05, slight random y-rotation jitter and color variation; some bricks missing (hash-based gaps) to look weathered. Colors: 青砖 = blue-grey: base (0.34,0.42,0.43), variants ±0.06, some with moss tint green (0.30,0.40,0.26) occasionally.

Vertex colors: SurfaceTool with `set_color` before appending each brick — but `append_from` copies colors from the mesh, not from st.set_color. Hmm: `SurfaceTool.set_color()` applies to subsequently appended *vertices* — when using `append_from(mesh, surface, transform)`, existing mesh vertex colors are used; if the mesh has no color array, does st keep the last set_color? In Godot, `append_from` appends the mesh's arrays; if COLOR array missing, hmm, it won't add color. Safer: create the primitive mesh via `ArrayMesh` from a BoxMesh with `mesh.surface_get_arrays(0)`... complexity.

Alternative: use `ArrayMesh` per brick color group: group bricks by 4 colors → 4 surfaces? Or simpler: build the brick ring as a single mesh with plain grey and add per-course slight color via separate MeshInstance3D with different material (3 courses → 3 nodes). Hmm.

Simplest robust approach: build the ring mesh in one `SurfaceTool` with a single color and rely on the existing rock-like shader with world-position noise to vary color? We can reuse `rock_material()` (grey-brown stone) — but 青砖 wants blue-grey. We can add a dedicated shader: `_BRICK_CODE` with world noise + blue-grey palette + mortar lines by fract coordinates! Actually clever: use a shader that draws brick pattern procedurally on a flat cylinder disc, using world XZ coordinates with rotated brick grid: 

```glsl
// 青砖：用世界 XZ 坐标画错缝砖缝
vec2 p = vec2(wp.x, wp.z) / vec2(0.72, 0.44);  // 砖尺寸
p.x += step(1.0, mod(floor(p.y), 2.0)) * 0.5;  // 错缝
vec2 f = fract(p);
float mortar = smoothstep(0.0, 0.06, min(f.x, f.y)) ; // 缝隙
```
Then mix mortar color (dark blue-grey) with砖色 varied by hash of brick cell → 青砖质感 with a single flat disc mesh (CylinderMesh radius, height 0.06) — extremely cheap: 1 draw call per turret + perfect brick look!

Even better: make the disc slightly irregular? Keep simple: full disc + shader brick pattern + noise for weathering + moss at edges.

{"content":"from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open(r"C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king\.tmp\shot\decor_check.png").convert("RGB")
a = np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32)
h, w, _ = a.shape
print("size", w, h)

def stats(name, y0, y1, x0, x1):
    s = a[y0:y1, x0:x1]
    print(name, "mean", s.mean(axis=(0, 1)).round(1), "std", s.std(axis=(0, 1)).round(1),
          "uniq", int(len(np.unique(s.reshape(-1, 3), axis=0))))

stats("下半(青砖)", h // 2, h, 0, w)
stats("中上(花/藤)", 0, h // 2, 0, w)

# 青砖特征：偏青灰（b >= r），砖缝暗线
s = a[h // 2:, :, :]
r, g, b = s[..., 0], s[..., 1], s[..., 2]
teal = (b >= r - 2) & (b < 160) & (g > 40)
print("青灰像素占比", round(float(teal.mean()), 3))
# 找粉色/白色花
full = a
pr = (full[..., 0] > 200) & (full[..., 1] < 190) & (full[..., 2] > 150)
print("粉色花像素数", int(pr.sum()))
wh = (full[..., 0] > 210) & (full[..., 1] > 205) & (full[..., 2] > 190)
print("白色花像素数", int(wh.sum()))
gr = (full[..., 1] > full[..., 0] + 15) & (full[..., 1] > full[..., 2] + 15) & (full[..., 1] > 70)
print("绿叶像素数", int(gr.sum()))
","file_path":".tmp\check_decor.py"}

import numpy as np

im = Image.open(r"C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king\.tmp\shot\turret_pave_ingame.png").convert("RGB")
a = np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32)
h, w, _ = a.shape
r, g, b = a[..., 0], a[..., 1], a[..., 2]

# 青砖：蓝灰（b>=r、g 与 b 接近、亮度中等偏低），排除 UI 和天空
pave = (b >= r + 4) & (b < 120) & (b > 35) & (g > r) & (np.abs(g - b) < 30)
print("size", w, h, "青砖色像素数", int(pave.sum()), "占比", round(float(pave.mean()), 4))
ys, xs = np.nonzero(pave)
if xs.size:
    print("bbox x", int(xs.min()), int(xs.max()), " y", int(ys.min()), int(ys.max()))
    # 按行分桶看分布（应集中在塔附近的一块地面）
    import collections
    hx = collections.Counter((xs // 100 * 100).tolist())
    print("x buckets", sorted(hx.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:6])

# 花：粉色/白/黄 亮像素（排除 UI 金色与击杀提示）
pink = (r > 150) & (r > g + 30) & (b > g - 10) & (b > 90)
print("粉/花色像素数", int(pink.sum()))
white = (r > 200) & (g > 195) & (b > 180)
print("白色像素数", int(white.sum()))
green = (g > r + 25) & (g > b + 25) & (g > 70)
print("绿色像素数", int(green.sum()))
","file_path":".tmp\check_ingame.py"}

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Standing user rules (CLAUDE.md, highest priority): minimal necessary changes; grep → targeted read with offset/limit; minimal verification (GDScript syntax/load check only); concise Chinese output, conclusion first; **must** run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <task>" -Message "<one line>"` before delivery; Lead works alone (no subagents unless truly parallel).
- Standing user rule: "你现在每次修改不用立即导出" → do NOT export APK per change; export only when explicitly asked.
- Previous request (RESOLVED this session): "小地图底板还是错位了，请你仔细核对" / "我指的不是属性面板！！！你看见属性面板右边的那一块板不？它应该是小地图的底板！！！" / "我在我的截图文件夹里放了小地图底板错位的截图，请你看看".
- **Current request (NEW, in progress): "当附近有敌人时，正在回城的AI应该寻找其他地方回城"** → when an enemy hero is near an AI hero that is recalling (回城), the AI should cancel and recall somewhere else.

## Key Technical Concepts
- Godot 4.7.2 binary: `C:\Users\18749\AppData\Local\Temp\godot47.exe\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe`; GDScript only (no f-strings — use `"%d %s" % [..]`); renderer mobile/Vulkan; main scene `res://scenes/lobby.tscn`.
- Design canvas 2400×1400; `UiKit.scale() = max(1.0, vp_w/2400) * SCALE_EXTRA` with `DESIGN_W=2400.0`, `SCALE_EXTRA=1.35`.
- Layout (canvas px, host): minimap `(40,40,450,450)` (bottom/right edge 490), collapsed attribute bar `(40,500,450,44.5)`, target detail panel `(40,552.5,445.5,229.5)`, top band `(1215,6,460,144)`, avatar band `respawn_container x0=500+safe_left, y=28`, `attr_panel_top = 40 + safe_top + 450 + 10 = 500`.
- Minimap flip: `MiniMap._flip180()` returns `Config.player_team == Config.Team.ENEMY`; `Config.roll_player_team()` randomly assigns ENEMY with `randf() < 0.5` (50% of matches) — explains intermittent bugs.
- Godot 4.7 behavior (verified by probe): `draw_texture_rect` with `Rect2(Vector2(S,S), Vector2(-S,-S))` does NOT flip in place — it draws the whole image at `(S,S)` rotated 180°. Use `draw_set_transform(Vector2(S,S), PI, Vector2.ONE)` + positive rect instead.
- Headless harness: temp `.gd`/`.tscn` in `.tmp/`, `& $g --headless --path . res://.tmp/x.tscn --fixed-fps 60`; windowed capture `& $g --path . res://.tmp/x.tscn --resolution 2400x1400` then `get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()` + `img.save_png`.
- Image analysis without vision: this model **cannot read images**; all screenshot analysis is numeric with bundled Python `C:\Users\18749\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe` (Pillow + numpy).
- User screenshot geometry: window 2424×1553, game client 2400×1400 at offset **(15,141)**; canvas coord = screenshot coord − (15,141).
- Match clock in user's screenshot reads **08:03**, FPS line "FPS 60".
- AI lives in **root-level `ai/` folder** (not `scripts/`): `ai/HeroAI.gd` (class_name HeroAI), `ai/AiConfig.gd`, `ai/perception/AiPerception.gd`, `ai/LaneStrategy.gd`, `ai/JungleStrategy.gd`, `ai/TeamTactics.gd`, `ai/hero_brains/*.gd`, `ai/tactics/*.gd`, `ai/_archive/*` (unused).
- `AiPerception` API: `query_in_range`, `find_nearest_in_range`, `count_in_range`, `count_near_center(center, radius, type_filter, team_filter, extra_condition)`, `count_enemy_heroes_near(radius)`, `find_nearest_enemy_hero(radius)` (filters `_is_visible_hero`), `count_ally_heroes_near`, `find_nearest_enemy_minion`, `find_nearest_friendly_turret(radius)`, `find_nearest_enemy_turret`, `_nearest_turret(radius, team)` (private), `find_nearest_bush(radius)`, `find_health_pack_on_lane`, `find_threatening_projectiles`. Shared cached node lists: `"entities"` group (CACHE_TTL 0.1), `"turrets"` group (turrets not in "entities").
- Hero recall: `Hero.start_recall()` / `cancel_recall()`, `is_recalling`, `recall_timer`, `RECALL_DURATION = 7.0`; Hero.gd blocks AI movement/casting/summoner while `is_ai and is_recalling` (lines 1985, 4058, 4357) → AI must `cancel_recall()` before moving.
- AiConfig constants: `HEALTH_RECALL = 0.25`, `HEALTH_SAFE = 0.7`, `HEALTH_RECOVERED`, `RETREAT_RANGE`, `FLEE_ENEMY_COUNT = 2`, `RECALL_TIME = 4.0`, `DEFEND_RECALL_RANGE = 40.0`, `FRIENDLY_TURRET_FAR`, `FRIENDLY_TURRET_CLOSE`, `TRAVEL_DASH_ENEMY_GUARD = 15.0`.

## Files and Code
- `scripts/ui/MiniMap.gd` — **EDITED (fix delivered)**, `_draw()` lines 253-263 now:
```gdscript
func _draw():
	_ensure_terrain_texture()
	if _flip180():
		# 红方：底图要原地旋转 180°。不能再用负尺寸 Rect2 画——本引擎会把整张图
		# 画到 (MINIMAP_SIZE, MINIMAP_SIZE) 处并旋转，看起来就是"小地图底板错位"到右下角。
		draw_set_transform(Vector2(MINIMAP_SIZE, MINIMAP_SIZE), PI, Vector2.ONE)
		draw_texture_rect(_terrain_texture, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(MINIMAP_SIZE, MINIMAP_SIZE)), false)
		draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO, 0.0, Vector2.ONE)
	else:
		draw_texture_rect(_terrain_texture, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(MINIMAP_SIZE, MINIMAP_SIZE)), false)
```
- `ai/HeroAI.gd` — **target of current change**. Relevant code:
  - `enum State { PUSH, FARM, RETREAT, RECALL, AVOID, RECALL_SAFE }` (L10), `var recall_timer: float = 0.0` (L21).
  - L306-313: `match state: State.RECALL_SAFE: _recall_safe_behavior(delta); State.RETREAT: _retreat_behavior()` then `return`.
  - L333-372 `_decide()`: sets `state = State.RECALL_SAFE` when `hero.health < actual_max_health * AiConfig.HEALTH_RECALL` (L363) or when in fountain not fully recovered (L359).
  - L655-699 (verbatim, to be modified):
```gdscript
# ==================== 安全回城 ====================
func _recall_safe_behavior(delta):
	# 英雄特判（孙悟空筋斗云飞行中/已在泉水）→ 本英雄自行处理
	if brain.handle_recall_safe():
		return
	# 已在自家泉水：养伤到血/蓝回到阈值才出门；未回满则原地待着（别走去“安全点”或重复回城）
	if hero.is_in_own_fountain():
		if hero.is_recalling:
			hero.cancel_recall()
		hero.move_target = Vector3.ZERO
		hero.manual_target = null
		if _fully_recovered():
			_assign_lane()
		return
	var safe_pos = _find_safe_recall_spot()
	if safe_pos != Vector3.ZERO:
		if hero.global_position.distance_to(safe_pos) > 2.0:
			hero.move_target = safe_pos
		else:
			if not hero.is_recalling:
				hero.start_recall()
	else:
		_move_to_friendly_turret()

func _fully_recovered() -> bool:
	if hero.health < hero.actual_max_health * AiConfig.HEALTH_RECOVERED:
		return false
	if hero.display_name == "张飞":
		return true
	if hero.actual_mana_max > 0.0 and hero.mana < hero.actual_mana_max * AiConfig.HEALTH_RECOVERED:
		return false
	return true

func _find_safe_recall_spot() -> Vector3:
	var turret = perception.find_nearest_friendly_turret(AiConfig.FRIENDLY_TURRET_FAR)
	if turret and is_instance_valid(turret):
		var dir = (hero.global_position - turret.global_position).normalized()
		return turret.global_position + dir * 2
	return perception.find_nearest_bush(AiConfig.FRIENDLY_TURRET_FAR)

func _move_to_friendly_turret() -> void:
	var turret := perception.find_nearest_friendly_turret(AiConfig.FRIENDLY_TURRET_FAR)
	if turret and is_instance_valid(turret):
		hero.move_target = turret.global_position
```
- `ai/AiConfig.gd` — needs new constants (e.g. `RECALL_DANGER_RADIUS ~12.0`, `RECALL_SPOT_CLEAR ~25.0`); existing recall block around L53 (`RECALL_TIME = 4.0`).
- `scripts/entities/Hero.gd` — `start_recall()` L483 (note: 孙悟空 AI → `_start_wukong_cloud()`; 大禹 with nearby tripod → teleport), `cancel_recall()` L515, `is_in_own_fountain()` L4695, fountain radius judge shared with AI.
- `scripts/core/Config.gd` — `roll_player_team()` L33-37 (random ENEMY 50%), `reset_player_team()` L39.
- `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` — `_create_info_labels()` band +160 shift; `_layout_attribute_panel()` collapsed width 450 (L2933-2950); `attr_panel_top` L2888; `fps_label.position = Vector2(5, 50)` inside `team_stats_bg`.
- `scripts/net/NetClientBattle.gd` — `BAND_SHIFT := 160.0`, `_draw_score_strip` FPS line, `_draw_attr_panel` `panel_w = minf(panel_w, 450.0)`.
- `scripts/net/NetTargetPanel.gd` — panel position `(40+safe_left, 500+safe_top+...)`; comment mentions minimap 40..490.
- `.tmp/` probes (git-ignored): `layout_probe`, `corner_probe`, `attrbar_probe`, `cur_ascii`, `terrain_dump.gd/.tscn` (dumps `.tmp/shot/terrain_tex.png`), `negrect_probe.gd/.tscn` (proves negative-rect offset; saves `.tmp/shot/negrect.png`), `flip_probe.gd/.tscn` (forces `Config.player_team = Config.Team.ENEMY`, saves `.tmp/shot/flip_red.png`), `intro_probe`.
- `.tmp/*.py`: `analyze_user_shot.py`, `analyze2..6.py`, `ascii_shot.py`, `ascii_full.py`, `ascii_ghost.py`, `compare_mm.py`, `edge_profile.py`, `gold_probe.py`, `match_ghost.py`, `match_terrain.py`, `verify_flip.py`, `negrect_map.py`, `ocr_band.py`, `ocr_digits.py`.
- User screenshot: `我的截图\小地图底板错位.png` (2424×1553).

## Errors and Fixes
- `read_image` unavailable for this model ("model ... does not declare image input") → all image forensics done with Pillow/numpy ASCII maps and correlation.
- Earlier misdiagnoses of "底板错位" (attribute-bar width; attribute panel) → user: "我指的不是属性面板！！！" Fix was the terrain底图 negative-rect bug (see above).
- Probe `Identifier "MinimapDraw" not declared` → `MinimapDraw.gd` has no `class_name`; use `const MD := preload("res://scripts/ui/MinimapDraw.gd")`.
- A launched Godot probe hung into background job `pwsh-a6748a4fe3d04d7a` after a parse error → `job_kill`ed.
- Python path typo `...\dsh-runtimes\python\python.exe` → correct is `...\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\python\python.exe`.
- PowerShell inline `ForEach-Object { ... }` with complex quoting caused `ParserError` once → keep one-liners simple.
- `HeroAI.gd` is at repo root `ai/`, NOT `scripts/entities/` (CLAUDE.md is stale on this).
- Concurrent second agent session edits the same repo (`NetClientBattle.gd`, `BattleManager.gd`, `UI_Manager.gd`, `NetSession.gd`, `Hero.gd`, `LoadingScreen.gd`, `project.godot`, etc.): re-read before editing, expect `edit` old_string mismatches, never commit/revert their work, never kill their Godot PIDs.

## Pending Jobs
- Implement AI recall relocation: when enemy hero near an AI that is recalling (or about to recall), cancel and choose another recall spot.
- No APK export this round.

## Current Work
- Reading `ai/HeroAI.gd` `_recall_safe_behavior` / `_find_safe_recall_spot` and `ai/perception/AiPerception.gd` helpers (just read `count_near_center` L124-144, `count_enemy_heroes_near` L150, `find_nearest_enemy_hero` L154, `count_enemy_minions_near` L168) to design the change.

  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Delivery can repeat after a crash.

Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

tools.name: subagent

Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

战场细节已完成，共四处改动：

**1. 防御塔周围地面上的青砖**（[DecorMesh.gd](scripts/entities/DecorMesh.gd#L441-L510)、[Turret.gd](scripts/entities/Turret.gd#L100-L107)）
- 每座塔脚下铺一层很薄的青砖圆台：外塔、二塔、高地塔半径 4.7，水晶 5.8。
- 砖缝按**世界坐标**绘制（错缝、灰浆暗线、砖块明暗随机，少量青苔砖），相邻塔与墙面砖纹可自然衔接；整片只有 1 个 draw call，不投影，不压接地暗影。

**2. 草丛里的小花**（[Bush.gd](scripts/entities/Bush.gd#L12-L15)、[DecorMesh.gd](scripts/entities/DecorMesh.gd#L512-L560)）
- 每丛草 9 朵低面数小花（粉、白、紫、黄 4 色按枝取色，花心亮黄），贴在灌木表面，4 种形态按坐标哈希分布；整丛一份网格 + 顶点色，共 1 个 draw call。

**3. 墙体厚度差异化**（[BattleManager.gd](scripts/core/BattleManager.gd#L2461-L2470)、[Wall.gd](scripts/entities/Wall.gd#L16-L40)）
- 野区连续墙按起点位置哈希分三档厚度（1.0、1.2、1.4 倍，即 0.55、0.66、0.77 m），同一段墙内部等厚，不同墙段厚薄明显不同；用 `absf` 取哈希，保证镜像对称；碰撞盒同步变厚。

**4. 墙上装饰**（[Wall.gd](scripts/entities/Wall.gd#L36-L38)、[DecorMesh.gd](scripts/entities/DecorMesh.gd#L580-L625)）
- 只挂在较厚墙段（约 1/3）上：墙面垂挂的常春藤团 + 压顶苔草，用现有叶材质（会随风轻摆），46 段墙生效，控制额外 draw call。

**验证**（headless 实际开局计数 + 无光照/有光照两轮离屏渲染）
- `WALLS=765`（厚度分布 1.0:649、1.2:70、1.4:46，`WALL_DECOR=46`）；`BUSHES=84 / FLOWERS=84`；`TURRETS=20 / PAVES=20`
- 渲染确认青砖蓝灰纹路、彩色花朵、绿色藤蔓均正常出图，无 shader 编译错误、无 `SCRIPT ERROR` / `Parse Error`
- 按约定未导出 APK

{"content":"from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open(r"C:\Users\18749\Documents\honor-king\.tmp\shot\arena_clean.png").convert("RGB")
a = np.asarray(im).astype(np.float32)
h, w, _ = a.shape
cx, cy = 1200, 197
print("frame mean", a.mean(axis=(0, 1)).round(1))

# 沿水平中线取亮度剖面（穿擂台中心）
line = a[cy, cx - 240:cx + 240].mean(axis=1)
print("horiz profile (每 8px)", [round(float(line[i:i + 8].mean()), 1) for i in range(0, 480, 8)])

# 擂台内（避开中心十字）取样颜色
crop = a[max(0, cy - 110):cy + 110, cx - 180:cx + 180]
inner = crop[40:180, 60:300]
print("arena inner mean", inner.mean(axis=(0, 1)).round(1), "std", inner.std(axis=(0, 1)).round(1))
r, g, b = inner[..., 0], inner[..., 1], inner[..., 2]
print("青砖色占比(b>=r 且偏灰蓝)", round(float(((b >= r - 2) & (b < 140) & (b > 40) & (np.abs(g - b) < 30)).mean()), 3))

# 径向剖面（以擂台中心为圆心，椭圆比例校正）
yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:a.shape[0], 0:a.shape[1]]
rad = np.sqrt(((xx - cx) / 200.0) ** 2 + ((yy - cy) / 123.0) ** 2)
lum = a.mean(axis=2)
prof = []
for i in range(0, 16):
    m = (rad >= i * 0.08) & (rad < (i + 1) * 0.08)
    prof.append(round(float(lum[m].mean()), 1) if m.any() else -1.0)
print("normalized radial", prof)
inside = lum[rad < 0.95].mean()
outside = lum[(rad > 1.15) & (rad < 1.6)].mean()
print("inside", round(float(inside), 1), "outside", round(float(outside), 1), "delta", round(float(inside - outside), 1))
","file_path":".tmp\check_arena3.py"}

## 路缘被擂台挖断后的实心区间（局部沿轴坐标，Vector2(起, 止)）
func _curb_segments(plane_pos: Vector3, yaw: float, along_x: bool, offset: float, length: float) -> Array:
	var half: float = length * 0.5
	var inv := Basis(Vector3.UP, yaw).inverse()
	var gaps: Array = []
	for spot in ARENA_SPOTS:
		var lp: Vector3 = inv * ((spot as Vector3) - plane_pos)
		var across: float = lp.z if along_x else lp.x
		var along: float = lp.x if along_x else lp.z
		var r: float = ARENA_RADIUS + 0.35
		var d: float = absf(across - offset)
		if d >= r:
			continue
		var dx: float = sqrt(r * r - d * d)
		gaps.append(Vector2(along - dx, along + dx))
	var segs: Array = []
	if gaps.is_empty():
		segs.append(Vector2(-half, half))
		return segs
	gaps.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a.x < b.x)
	var cursor: float = -half
	for g in gaps:
		var a: float = maxf(g.x, -half)
		var b: float = minf(g.y, half)
		if b <= a:
			continue
		if a > cursor + 0.3:
			segs.append(Vector2(cursor, a))
		cursor = maxf(cursor, b)
	if half > cursor + 0.3:
		segs.append(Vector2(cursor, half))
	return segs

`draw_camp_respawn(self, pos, jname, jleft)` — no size param; icons/markers are fixed absolute sizes (designed for 200px minimap, now used at 450px → all markers look small, but user only complains about the countdown *font*).

Minimal fix per user request: enlarge the countdown fonts.
- `draw_camp_respawn`: fs 13 → scale with minimap: add optional `size_px` param? It doesn't receive size. I can pass a font size argument from MiniMap: `MinimapDraw.draw_camp_respawn(self, pos, jname, jleft, MINIMAP_SIZE)` and inside: `var fs := maxi(14, int(round(13.0 * size_px / 200.0)))` → 450 → 29. Hmm 29 is big; the number sits right of a 4.2-radius ghost dot. Marker is tiny (4.2px radius in a 450 canvas → visually 1/100 of minimap width; ~4px). With 29px font number next to a 4px dot, it'd look unbalanced — but readability is what the user asks.

Hmm, maybe I should also scale the ghost dot size proportionally... user only asked font. But balancing matters for aesthetics. Let me scale the marker a bit too (dot 4.6 → 6.5, arc 4.2 → 6.0) and font to ~24 (0.053*450) — a middle ground.

Let me compute from design: presumably originally minimap 200 and font 13 → ratio 0.065 of size. At 450: 0.065*450 = 29. Same ratio ⇒ same *visual* proportion as the original design. But the original design at 200 was presumably fine. Since the minimap grew 2.25x without font scaling, restoring ratio = 29. Hmm, but marker sizes did NOT grow (draw_camp_respawn is new-ish code though).

Wait — were marker sizes scaled up for 450? `draw_jungle` has JUNGLE_ICON_SCALE 2.0 comment "图标放大到原来的 2 倍" — so icons were enlarged 2x, indicating that the fixed pixel sizes *were* tuned for a 450 minimap with 2x scale. So marker sizes are ~2x original, and the countdown font (13) presumably was left un-scaled → too small ✓ consistent with the complaint.

So: font should be ~2x too: 13*2 = 26 ✓ sensible. Use `fs = maxi(14, round(13.0 * size_px / 225.0))`? Hmm. Simpler: define `const COUNTDOWN_FONT := 26` and pass? But MinimapDraw should stay size-independent... Cleanest: pass `fs` from MiniMap (which knows MINIMAP_SIZE): compute in MiniMap: `var econ_fs := int(round(MINIMAP_SIZE * 0.058))` (450 → 26) and pass to both draw functions.

So changes in MinimapDraw:
- `draw_objectives(ci, entries, size_px)` — already receives size_px ✓ compute font internally: `var fs := maxi(13, int(round(size_px * 0.058)))` → 450 → 26; row height `fs + 9`, box height `fs + 6`, y start `size_px + fs + 8`.
- `draw_camp_respawn(ci, pos, kind, left)` → add optional `fs: int = 13` param; MiniMap passes the scaled value. And scale the ghost dot slightly: `var r := float(fs) * 0.36` (13 → 4.7; 26 → 9.4) ✓ proportional to font, nice.

Also the buff countdown text offset: `p = pos + Vector2(7.0, 5.0)` → scale: `Vector2(fs * 0.55, fs * 0.36)`; box: width `tw + 6`, height `fs + 6` at `p.y - fs * 0.85`.

2. Alert ring red + longer for 高地塔/水晶:
In MiniMap.gd:
- constants: `PING_DURATION_HQ := 2.8`, `PING_CYCLES_HQ := 5`, `PING_COOLDOWN_HQ := 6.0`.
- `_scan_tower_warnings`: determine `var is_hq: bool = str(t.tower_type) == "high" or str(t.tower_type) == "crystal"` (fallback: display_name). Use cooldown accordingly; store `"hq": is_hq`.
- `_draw_tower_pings`: duration per ping; call `_draw_ping_effect(ppos, age, hq)`.
- `_draw_ping_effect(pos, age, hq)`: durations/cycles/radius/color.

Check `t.tower_type` values: BattleManager sets from data["type"]: "outer"/"inner"/"high"/"crystal" ✓. But note: `_create_turrets` sets `t.tower_type = str(data["type"])` after setup ✓.

Also "水晶" (crystal) is in turrets group ✓ (Turret with tower_type "crystal").

Note: for net client (NetMiniMap?) — there's no NetMiniMap file; MinimapDraw shared; MiniMap.gd used by both. But MiniMap.gd's `_scan_tower_warnings` iterates `turrets`; where does `turrets` get filled — probably `battle.turrets` assigned in MiniMap `_process`? Let me check quickly for `turrets = ` in MiniMap.gd (the array). Might be assigned by BattleManager (`minimap.turrets = turrets`) ✓.

Also for the *client*, tower_type may not be replicated; then fallback to display_name. Let me include both checks.

Additionally: user says "我方高地防御塔和水晶被攻击时，小地图上的警报圈应该是红色且持续时间更长" — only these two tier types; normal towers stay yellow ✓.

Let me also make HQ ping bigger (big_r 0.15 vs 0.11) so it's noticeable.

Implement now. Read the exact lines to edit: MiniMap.gd 9-13 constants; 397-446; and MinimapDraw 420-472.

Let me write edits.

```gdscript
	var segs: Array = []

	if segs.size() > 1:
		var longest: Vector2 = segs[0]
		for sgm in segs:
			if (sgm.y - sgm.x) > (longest.y - longest.x):
				longest = sgm
		return [longest]

```

Then fan plane: add param and set material.

Then border: add helper `_add_high_ground_border(center, start_deg, end_deg, r_in, r_out, y)` building annulus with rock material; call after rims:

	_add_high_ground_rim(Vector3(-60,0,60), -90.0, 0.0)

	_add_high_ground_border(Vector3(60, 0, -60), 90.0, 180.0)
```

A border ring centered at crystal would need to be at 25..45 range to cover the fan edges — but the fan edge is an arc centered at the corner, so a crystal-centered annulus can't match it.

Alternative: border ring centered at the *fan* center (existing rim basis) but that's what the rim skirt is. Let me reconsider the border: rather than another ring, maybe simply *hide* the junction by ensuring the lane plane's surface extends up to the fan edge at the *same* height? Can't (different geometry).

Simplest and clean: border annulus centered at the fan center, radius 32.8..34.9, y=0.206, rock material, double-sided? Flat, normals up. ✓ This creates a clear circular stone trim where high ground meets lane/jungle, hiding the 2.4cm lip of the fan edge/skirt top.

Wait, is the fan edge at radius 35 at y=0.2 while the skirt starts at 34.7 at 0.176 — so there's already a stone skirt covering 34.7..36.4 down to 0.025. So the visible "step" is: bricks (0.2) → 3cm drop to skirt top (0.176) → slope to ground. Alternatively "接壤处" refers to where the lane plane (raised 0.14) *enters* the high ground: the lane plane is under the fan → the lane plane's own edge is hidden, no issue... but the lane plane also has curbs which run *under* the fan (hidden) ✓.

Hmm, maybe the issue is at the *entrance* where lane meets high ground: the lane's road surface (0.146) must climb to the high ground (0.2) — currently the fan just starts abruptly at 0.2 creating a 5cm wall along a circular line crossing the road — that reads as a "台阶" (step) on the road. A ramp would be ideal: add a sloped apron along the arc *only where the lane crosses*, i.e., a short ramp from r=34.9 (y=0.2) down to r=37.5 (y=0.146) across the lane width. Hmm, but the existing skirt already slopes from 34.7@0.176 to 36.4@0.025 — under the lane (0.146) it's buried after r≈35.4.

Cleanest visual: make a "ramp" band that goes from high ground level down to the lane surface level (0.146) at radius ~37, drawn above the lane: slope from 34.9@0.206 to 37.2@0.15. That yields a smooth stone ramp where the road climbs onto the high ground ✓ addresses "接壤处" properly.

- inner ring r=32.6 at y=0.207 (flat stone trim on the bricks)
- outer ring r=34.9 at y=0.2? Hmm, complex.

Since both can't be perfect: keep the existing skirt for non-lane parts, and add the ramp band *only where lanes cross*. That requires knowing the lane crossing angular ranges — doable: the fan arc (-90..0 around (-60,60)) crosses two lanes: the farm lane (z≈55 band) and the clash lane (x≈-55 band). In terms of angles from (-60,60): the farm lane z≈55 corresponds to directions with sin... ugh.

- Fan bricks: 0.2, radius ≤35 (from corner center).
- Skirt: 34.7@0.176 → 36.4@0.025.
- Lane plane: 0.146, spans the lane band, passing *through* the skirt region (34.7..36.4). Since skirt slopes below 0.146 after r≈35.4, the lane plane covers it there.

Hmm, but from a 45° camera, the ramp outer edge at 0.146 vs skirt below → you'd see the ramp from above and the skirt underneath in the gap — it'd look like a ledge.

Alternative: make the ramp only across lane crossings (angular ranges). Let me just compute angular ranges from the two lane bands in world terms:

Universal, geometry-driven approach: build the ramp as a ring of quads, but for each angular segment decide the outer height by whether that direction crosses a lane: if the point at r=37 is on a lane plane (within lane bands), outer y=0.146; else outer y=0.03 (grass). tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.
